Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0124", "row_sha256": "dfac7a1cebff2e1df944fdc8f6bf2b8428e20dc4c9c3410b97f54fab17b96fb9", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "i need a prompt for a clear inventory report for the cedar street food cooperative, using the count from monday march 25 and the ledger activity posted through sunday march 24. keep it to this inventory snapshot, not a general review of the coop or a purchasing plan. the report is for Orson, not Nadia. Nadia usually handles supplier orders, but Orson is the person who asked for this count summary. please make the prompt say who the report is for so it doesn't get routed to the wrong person. the stock was checked in the pantry, walk-in cooler, freezer and the small receiving area beside the rear door. use the figures below and keep the location attached to each item; people sometimes move things between the pantry and receiving area before shelving them.

in the pantry the physical count found 42 one-kilogram bags of dried chickpeas, while the ledger showed 48. there was no note on the count sheet explaining the difference, so don't supply a reason for it. for long-grain rice, eleven 25-kilogram sacks were counted and the ledger had ten. canned tomatoes were counted as 96 tins in total, compared with 100 on the ledger; twelve of the tins were dented and set aside, so make that distinction clear rather than describing all 96 as saleable stock. the pantry also had 7 jars of tahini, but the ledger entry is in kilograms and says 5.5 kg. no one weighed the jars during this count, so those are not directly comparable units. please don't convert them to an estimated number of jars or kilograms.

in the walk-in cooler there were 18 returnable bottles of whole milk and the ledger listed 20. the date printed on the bottles is march 26. there were 23 tubs of plain yogurt physically present, against 24 in the ledger, and the tubs have a march 28 date. don't call either product expired: the count was march 25. there were also two open cases of spinach, with 6 bags in one and 5 in the other; the ledger records 12 bags received but has no separate use or waste entry. the count sheet doesn't say whether a bag was taken out earlier, so report the count and the ledger figure without guessing what happened to the missing bag.

in the freezer the volunteers counted 14 bags of frozen blueberries, each labeled 2 pounds, and the ledger showed 14 bags as well. three of those bags have a torn outer wrap, though the inner sealed bags looked intact. the person counting them wrote that they remain in the freezer and did not move them to the discard bin. frozen vegetable cases were not opened, and their quantities were read from the outside labels: 8 cases of peas and 6 of mixed vegetables. the ledger has 8 and 7 respectively. make clear that the case counts came from labels, not from opening and counting individual bags. no weight check was done for the frozen stock.

at receiving there were 4 crates of apples waiting to be put away. the delivery slip is dated march 25 and lists 5 crates; one crate was marked as left at the neighboring bakery on the driver copy, but the cooperative copy has no signature beside that note. Lupe said, "the crates by the back door are not counted yet," when the volunteers began, and then the four crates were added to the physical count. include that quote as a note about the count process, not as proof of a delivery shortage. there were also 3 cartons of oat milk on the receiving shelf with no matching delivery slip in the folder. they appear on the ledger as 3 cartons received on march 24. don't claim they came in on the 25th or identify a supplier when the papers don't say.

please have the prompt request a short opening that gives the count date, ledger cutoff, and the four locations checked, followed by a numbered section for the item-by-item comparison. a compact table would help: item, location, physical count, ledger entry, and a notes or status field. retain units exactly as recorded, and show any difference only where units make a direct comparison possible. for apples, mention both the four crates present and the delivery slip's five, with the unsigned note about the neighboring bakery kept as an unresolved document detail. for the tahini, show the count and ledger units separately. don't calculate a variance between jars and kilograms. identify dented or torn packaging as observed condition, without changing the quantities or deciding that stock is unusable.

there are a few counting limitations to include in a brief methods note. the pantry and cooler items were counted individually, except the spinach bags were counted within the two open cases. the frozen peas and mixed vegetables were counted from case labels, not from the contents. the receiving-area apples were physically counted after the volunteers started, and the delivery paperwork has the unsigned note described above. there was no weighing of tahini jars or frozen stock, no note explaining the chickpea difference, and no spinach use or waste entry. keep those points separate from confirmed quantities, and don't fill any gaps with an explanation. distinguish physical counts, ledger entries, and information copied from labels or paperwork wherever that matters.

finish with a separate paragraph noting that the pantry scale's calibration sticker says it was last checked on february 12, while the cooler thermometer log has entries through march 24 and no entry for march 25. these are equipment and record details only; the count sheet doesn't say either affected the quantities. mention them without drawing a conclusion. the volunteer roster lists the next inventory shift for thursday march 28 at 4 p.m., with Orson scheduled to open the store room. keep that as scheduling information at the end, and don't add recommendations, approvals, or a claim that the ledger has been corrected.", "output": "Create a concise inventory report for the Cedar Street Food Cooperative, addressed to Orson, not Nadia. Use the physical count taken on Monday, March 25, and ledger activity posted through Sunday, March 24. Cover only this inventory snapshot, not a general review or purchasing plan. The four locations checked were the pantry, walk-in cooler, freezer, and receiving area beside the rear door. Keep each item's location clear.

Begin with the count date, ledger cutoff, and locations checked. Then provide a numbered item-by-item comparison, preferably in a compact table with columns for item, location, physical count, ledger entry, and notes or status. Retain units exactly as recorded. Show differences only when the units allow a direct comparison; do not infer missing information or explain discrepancies without evidence.

1. **Pantry**
   - Dried chickpeas: 42 one-kilogram bags physically counted; ledger shows 48. The count sheet gives no explanation for the difference.
   - Long-grain rice: 11 sacks of 25 kilograms physically counted; ledger shows 10.
   - Canned tomatoes: 96 tins physically counted; ledger shows 100. Of the 96 tins, 12 were dented and set aside. Distinguish those tins from the rest without describing all 96 as saleable stock.
   - Tahini: 7 jars physically counted; ledger entry is 5.5 kg. Show the recorded units separately. The jars were not weighed, so do not convert between jars and kilograms or calculate a variance.

2. **Walk-in cooler**
   - Whole milk: 18 returnable bottles physically counted; ledger shows 20. The bottles are dated March 26.
   - Plain yogurt: 23 tubs physically counted; ledger shows 24. The tubs are dated March 28. The count was on March 25, so do not call either product expired.
   - Spinach: two open cases contained 6 bags and 5 bags, respectively. The ledger records 12 bags received and has no separate use or waste entry. Report the physical count and ledger figure without guessing what happened to the difference.

3. **Freezer**
   - Frozen blueberries: 14 bags labeled 2 pounds each were physically counted; ledger shows 14 bags. Three bags had torn outer wraps, but their inner sealed bags looked intact. They remained in the freezer and were not moved to the discard bin.
   - Frozen peas: 8 cases counted from the outside labels; ledger shows 8.
   - Mixed vegetables: 6 cases counted from the outside labels; ledger shows 7.
   State that the vegetable case counts came from labels, not from opening and counting individual bags. No weight check was done for frozen stock.

4. **Receiving area beside the rear door**
   - Apples: 4 crates were physically present and counted. The March 25 delivery slip lists 5 crates. The driver copy says one crate was left at the neighboring bakery, but the cooperative copy has no signature beside that note. Include the paperwork detail as unresolved, not as proof of a delivery shortage. Lupe said, “the crates by the back door are not counted yet,” when volunteers began; the four crates were then added to the physical count. Present the quote as a note about the count process, not evidence of a shortage.
   - Oat milk: 3 cartons were on the receiving shelf without a matching delivery slip in the folder. The ledger lists 3 cartons received on March 24. Do not say they arrived on March 25 or identify a supplier.

Add a brief methods note, separate from the confirmed quantities. Pantry and cooler items were counted individually, except spinach bags were counted within the two open cases. Peas and mixed vegetables were counted from case labels. The receiving-area apples were counted after volunteers began, and the delivery paperwork contains the unsigned note described above. Tahini jars and frozen stock were not weighed. The count sheet offers no explanation for the chickpea difference, and there is no spinach use or waste entry. Distinguish physical counts, ledger entries, and information copied from labels or paperwork where relevant; do not fill gaps with explanations.

End with a separate paragraph on these equipment and scheduling details: the pantry scale's calibration sticker says it was last checked on February 12; the cooler thermometer log has entries through March 24 but none for March 25. The count sheet does not say that either detail affected the quantities, so report them without drawing a conclusion. The volunteer roster lists the next inventory shift for Thursday, March 28, at 4 p.m., with Orson scheduled to open the store room. Keep this scheduling information at the end. Do not add recommendations, approvals, or a claim that the ledger has been corrected."}]
